They derive a closed-form, piecewise polynomial formula for the Radon transform of an axis-aligned cube in any dimension. Their discrete transform is analytically exact for voxelized data and computationally efficient. A regularized variant swaps the slice area for the volume of a thin slab. Tests cover 3D shape matching and classification.
arxiv-2603-13603: Matthew Alford proves what he calls the Equivalence Theorem for database systems. He argues that a structurally complete system for knowledge representation needs exactly four capabilities. They are n-ary relationships with attributes, temporal validity, uncertainty quantification, and causal links between relationships. Any system with one of them needs all four, and a system that lacks one cannot be complete, he claims. He builds a framework, the Attributed Temporal Causal Hypergraph, that has all four at once. It ranks above SQL, LPG, and TypeDB in expressiveness.
arxiv-2603-13803: Vinaykumar and Kamasani present ALTIS, a pipeline that scores flood damage house by house from satellite radar. Radar sees through clouds, so maps can be ready within a day or two of a flood peak. ALTIS mixes change detection, depth estimates from terrain data, and parcel records for each property. Depth-damage links are tuned against real insurance claims from the national flood program. The output is a ranked triage list with confidence scores, tested on Hurricane Harvey data from Harris County, Texas.
arxiv-2603-14103: Hariri, Hinczewski, and Chaudhary present Scorio.jl, a Julia package for ranking systems from repeated task responses. One tensor-based interface hosts many ranking styles: direct scores, pairwise matches, psychometric models, voting, graph methods, and listwise rules. The same benchmark can thus be read under several ranking assumptions. The authors set the package beside existing Julia tools. Pilot tests cover rank recovery on synthetic data, stability with few trials, and runtime scaling.
arxiv-2603-14303: Wu and co-authors present SemantiCache, a way to shrink the KV cache of language models without shredding meaning. Token-level cuts can split coherent text units and lose facts for good. SemantiCache first chunks the cache at natural text boundaries. A greedy seed clustering step then groups tokens into meaning clusters inside each chunk. Merged cores get a proportional attention fix to restore their lost weight. Tests show decoding about 2.6 times faster with much lower memory and near-equal quality.
arxiv-2603-14503: Royo and co-authors map dark matter in galaxy clusters with diffusion models. Cluster mass, about 85% dark matter, bends light from background galaxies. Rebuilding that mass at survey scale has lacked fast tools and big test sets. The team builds DarkClusters-15k, a set of 15,000 simulated clusters with mass and light maps. A diffusion prior trained on the set guides reconstructions from lensing data. The method needs no hand tuning and runs in minutes. It matches expert results on the MACS 1206 cluster, they report.
arxiv-2603-14803: Oh, Seol and Kim extract a target voice from mixtures across all overlap ratios with VorTEX. Text-prompted extraction often assumes voices overlap in full. Real speech overlaps in part, and behavior there stays unclear. PORTE, a built two-speaker dataset, sweeps overlap from 0% to 100%. A decoupled fusion block splits extraction from side regularization paths. A new score, SuRE, flags suppression that standard metrics miss. VorTEX tops fidelity from 20% to 100% overlap, they report. Zero SuRE shows no suppression tricks at play.
arxiv-2603-15703: D'Onofrio and co-authors release py5vec, a Python package for continuous wave searches. The package implements the 5-vector method for faint, steady gravitational wave signals. It also reviews the method's theory in full. Two extensions marginalize over noise variance and starting phase. The first gives a sturdier Student's t likelihood. The second guards against pulsar glitches. A modular layout splits data handling, demodulation, and inference. Searches on LIGO O4a data rebuilt injected signals well.
arxiv-2603-15803: Ma and co-authors fix a waste in diffusion language model training. Standard training masks tokens at random, with no sense of density. Glue words then eat training effort while logic hubs starve. Their smart noise scheduler scores information density first. Complementary Priority Masking splits each case into twin samples. One sample stresses reasoning hubs, the other syntax basics. Accuracy rose about 4 percent on four code and math tests. The masking also curbs context collapse in block training.
arxiv-2603-16303: Li and co-authors release eAP, a large dataset for event-based driving perception. Normal cameras fail in harsh light, but event cameras cope better. No large event dataset existed for self-driving scenes. eAP is the largest such set so far. With it, the team improved a known 3D vehicle detector under hard lighting. They also built the best event-based time-to-contact estimator, running at 200 frames per second. Data, code, and trained models will be public.
arxiv-2603-16803: Subedi Chhetri and co-authors build a low-cost syringe pump system for soft robots. Their target robots, Silibots, are silicone voxel robots that change shape as voxels inflate and deflate. Standard air supplies are costly, imprecise, or complex. The new pumps use off-the-shelf and 3D printed parts. Each pump can push air in and also pull a vacuum, which most systems cannot do. The modular hardware and custom software let users run several pumps at once, each with its own settings.
arxiv-2603-17003: Gadginmath, Allibhoy, and Pasqualetti propose a control method that drives a system into a safe set by a set deadline. Their tool is a constricting control barrier function. A safety tube starts wide enough to hold the initial state, then shrinks to the target set at the deadline. Any controller that keeps the tube invariant reaches safety on time. Unlike older prescribed time methods, control effort stays bounded. Feasibility reduces to one checkable condition on the shrink rate. They validate the method on an 18 dimensional multi agent system.
arxiv-2603-17303: Han and co-authors present CulT-Eval, a benchmark for cultural understanding in machine translation. Idioms, slang, and culture specific items carry meanings past their literal form, and translation systems often miss them. Prior benchmarks are fragmented, with no shared scheme for such expressions. CulT-Eval holds over 7,959 curated instances across many types of culturally grounded expressions, with a detailed error taxonomy. Tests of large language models reveal recurring failure modes that standard metrics miss. The authors add a metric aimed at culturally induced meaning drift.
arxiv-2603-17403: Shi and co-authors present GMFlow, a model that synthesizes 3D earthquake ground motion at regional scale. Hazard work needs large sets of shaking records, but physics runs cost too much. GMFlow uses flow matching in a latent space shaped by physical parameters. On Bay Area scenarios it filled over nine million grid points in seconds. That ran about ten thousand times faster than the simulation workflow, they report.
arxiv-2603-17803: Wang, Chu, Fan, and Ren present Swarm, a system that parks language-model KV caches on SSD arrays. GPU memory fills fast, and DRAM offload still caps size and cost. Single SSD reads stall on bus bandwidth instead. Real workloads reuse stable clusters of cache entries together, they find. Swarm spreads those clusters across many drives for parallel reads. I/O time fell by 2.41 times in their tests.
arxiv-2603-17903: Aoude, Elkhidir, Ilderton, O'Connell, and Rajeev revisit quantum field theory on a background through amplitudes. Scattering methods now describe black hole backgrounds that shed gravitational waves. They read Bogoliubov coefficients as generalized amplitudes in that frame. Crossing, analyticity, and causality then link the full amplitude set, they explain. When the background is a coherent state, the story maps onto flat-space results. The review ties old formalism to new practice.
arxiv-2603-18303: Ismailzadeh and Ravan propose multi-outcome circuit optimization for non-Gaussian photonic state generation. Standard circuits herald one target outcome and waste other useful measurement patterns. Their strategy lets one circuit yield useful states across several patterns at once. Tests cover GKP core states, cat states, binomial codes, and cubic phase states. Gains come from targeting diverse states together and from pooling degenerate outcomes for one target.
arxiv-2603-18903: Baldassarri and de Jongh study how a controller can steer a cold magnetic lattice model to a fully filled state. Particles move under Kawasaki rules, and the system tends to stall in trapped states. They frame the task as a Markov decision process on states with one cluster. They solve for the best policy under two reward types. A time-only reward grows the cluster from edge centers. An energy-cost reward grows it from the corners instead.
arxiv-2603-19003: Kang and Liu study the best pairing pattern in a random monomer-dimer model on branching trees. Each edge and site gets a random weight, and the ground state pairs or leaves sites to gain the most weight. They work on a class of random rooted trees with weights drawn apart. They prove the tree's ground state is almost surely the only one and can be guessed from local data. Ground states on large finite graphs then settle to the tree state. A strong decorrelation trait follows from the result.
arxiv-2603-19203: Fan and co-authors show that the wording of a question can blind vision-language models to the image. Even when two wordings need the same visual work, closed forms draw far less attention to the picture. Multiple choice and yes-no prompts shift focus away from key regions. The team traces most of the accuracy loss to this misplaced attention. They add a light prompt-tuning fix with learned tokens. It restores the stronger gaze seen with open prompts and lifts scores across forms.
arxiv-2603-19403: Ge and co-authors test how well trial and person level links validate a binary stand-in endpoint. A yes-no endpoint can be read early, unlike the true time-to-event outcome. Regulators need proof that such a stand-in truly tracks the real endpoint. The standard meta-analytic method has not faced a full simulation check for binary cases. The team varies trial design choices in simulations to grade the estimates. The work shows when the validation numbers can be trusted.
arxiv-2603-19603: Saeedi and co-authors study how nearby features change the pressure needed for elastic cavitation. Cavitation is the sudden growth of a cavity in a soft solid under load. For a lone cavity in a neo-Hookean solid, the classic threshold is well known. A nearby rigid wall raises the threshold as the cavity gets closer. At the wall, it nears the known interface value. A neighbouring cavity gives a non-monotonic pattern instead. The peak sits at a gap of about four cavity radii.
arxiv-2603-19803: Tsai and co-authors revisit three open questions about the temperate sub-Neptune K2-18 b. New JWST spectra have sparked debate over claimed dimethyl sulfide signals. The team couples climate and photochemical models in a self-consistent way. They assume a moderate orbital eccentricity of 0.2. New lab measures of DMS and DMDS infrared opacity feed the study. Updated ethane opacity data are compiled as well. Their results support a sub-Neptune reading without invoking DMS. They find no strong evidence for a water-rich interior.
arxiv-2603-20103: Azad and co-authors use temporal abstraction to fix a spectral mismatch in forward-backward representations. These representations factor the successor representation in continuous spaces. Real transition dynamics are high rank, while the model forces a low rank form. The authors show abstraction acts like a low pass filter on the spectrum. It cuts the effective rank while keeping a bound on value error. Empirically, this alignment steadies learning, above all at high discount factors. Bootstrapping gets error prone there, so the effect matters most.
arxiv-2603-20503: Chen and co-authors use perturbation duality to give short, general proofs in robust optimization. Duality underpins both theory and tractable reformulations in this field. Standard proofs lean on minimax arguments or conic duality instead. Their perturbation route yields new theorems for a unifying DRO framework. That framework joins divergence and Wasserstein models under moment constraints. They resolve an open conjecture by replacing compactness with regularity conditions. They also unify dual-best forms of robust duality using bifunctions. The results streamline several recent proofs in the literature.
arxiv-2603-20803: Wiggins builds a geometric test for how sensitive a quantum system is to small changes in how it is prepared. The usual tool for scrambling, the OTOC, is algebraic and hard to picture. His test uses Bohmian paths and Lagrangian descriptors to give that sensitivity a shape. Wavepackets are labeled by start center and momentum kick. For the inverted harmonic oscillator the math can be done in closed form. Sensitivity grows at an exponential rate away from the origin. He sets this beside OTOC growth.
arxiv-2603-21003: Wang and co-authors propose erasure conversion for integer fluxonium qubits. They work with two qubit transitions that are both first order insensitive to flux noise. The main error in each is energy relaxation, which can be recast as an erasure event. Erasure events are easier for quantum error correcting codes to handle than general errors. Their protocol uses dispersive readout to detect these events. With well chosen circuit parameters and gate sets, they find these qubits promise high effective coherence times.
arxiv-2603-21103: Ekşi and Bakır explain the strong internal magnetic fields of central compact objects. These young neutron stars sit in supernova remnants and look radio quiet. Their surface dipole fields seem weak, yet X-ray data imply much stronger fields inside. The authors argue the dipole field is close to what flux conservation passed down from the progenitor's core. Slow initial spin blocks the alpha process. A full dynamo cannot run, but the omega effect can still build strong toroidal fields.
arxiv-2603-21203: Streltsov and co-authors show orbital-selective electron behavior in the kagome magnet YMn6Sn6. The kagome lattice hosts flat bands and Dirac fermions, but orbital-selective phases there were an open question. They combine resonant inelastic X-ray scattering with density functional and dynamical mean-field theory. Some manganese orbitals, aimed along bonds, form coherent metallic quasiparticles. Others, aimed at ligands, turn strongly correlated and show non-Fermi-liquid behavior. Hund's exchange freezes orbital fluctuations and locks in the split. The split also explains the ferromagnetic coupling between bilayers.
arxiv-2603-21403: Spinellis and Kotti argue that software engineering research faces a structural squeeze. For decades the field used open tools and systems that were easy to study at small scale. Many key systems today are large, closed, and rooted in industry settings that academics cannot reach. Small tweaks to method will not fix this, they say. They urge industrial PhDs, lasting industry partnerships, bigger teams, moonshot projects, and changes in funding and review.
arxiv-2603-21703: Jüttner and Buchmann review what governments tell smart home users after a cyberattack. Compromised residents tend to turn to official sources, so the quality of that guidance matters. They screened government cybersecurity sources across eleven countries with a standardized process. Three clusters emerged: incident reporting, general security advice, and incident response. Reporting channels and preventive tips were plentiful. Step-by-step recovery guidance for non-experts was rare, appearing in only two sources. The authors flag a gap between prevention advice and post-incident support for smart home users.
arxiv-2603-22003: Wang and co-authors present VP-VLA, a framework that helps robots follow language instructions. Most vision-language-action models map images and commands straight to control signals in one pass. VP-VLA splits the job in two. A planner breaks the task into sub-tasks and marks target objects and goal spots. Those marks are drawn on the camera image as crosshairs and boxes. A controller then uses the marked image to act. The authors report better results than QwenOFT and GR00T-N1.6 in tests.
arxiv-2603-22103: Upravitelev and co-authors treat differing readings of a story as a resource, not a flaw. Judging narrative similarity is interpretive work. Two valid readings of one text can give different similarity scores. The team builds an ensemble of 31 language model personas. Some follow named interpretive frameworks, while others read in a lay style. On the SemEval-2026 Task 4 data, the ensemble scores 0.705 accuracy. Accuracy grows with ensemble size, and practitioner personas help most in majority voting.
arxiv-2603-23203: Hoang and co-authors tackle impedance identification for inverter-based resources in modern power grids. These devices use varied controls, so their impedance behavior differs a lot from unit to unit. Training one model per device does not scale well. The team groups devices with K-means clustering, then trains a small feed-forward network for each cluster. In use, a few measurements predict impedance across many operating points. Tests on six devices, plus one unseen device with just ten points, show high accuracy.
arxiv-2603-23403: Yoshii and Oto study a Kondo effect born from a topological soliton. The soliton sits in a one-dimensional Dirac system with a sign-changing mass term. It hosts a localized zero mode with a spread-out wavefunction. That spread makes the exchange coupling to passing electrons depend on momentum. High-energy scattering gets filtered out, so the effective Kondo coupling varies with energy. The soliton's real-space shape thus sets the emergent Kondo scale. The pair frame this as a route to engineer many-body scales through topology.
arxiv-2603-24403: Roy and co-authors study how public opinion and vaccination shape epidemic spread on uneven networks. In their coupled model, opinions drive the chance that a person vaccinates, and opinions shift through peer contact and local risk perception from nearby infection rates. They place the dynamics on scale-free Barabási-Albert networks. Using Monte Carlo simulations and a Markov-chain method, they derive the critical infection threshold. Stronger local risk perception boosts pro-vaccine views and cuts infection, while peer influence alone can raise long-term infection.
arxiv-2603-24503: Clement and co-authors propose Sequential-AMPC, a learning-based way to speed up nonlinear model predictive control. Solving a nonlinear program online is costly on embedded hardware, and learned policies usually need huge expert datasets. Their neural policy shares parameters across the prediction horizon and generates candidate control sequences step by step. A safe variant adds an online evaluation and fallback layer for deployment. Across benchmarks, it needs far fewer expert rollouts than a feedforward baseline, yields more feasible sequences, and learns faster on high-dimensional systems.
arxiv-2603-24703: Xavier and co-authors present IndustriConnect, a prototype suite of adapters linking AI assistants to plant systems. Assistants cannot natively speak Modbus, MQTT/Sparkplug B, or OPC UA. Their adapters expose plant operations as tools an AI can find by schema, while keeping protocol-specific safety controls. A mock-first workflow lets adapter behaviour be tested locally before plant connection. A benchmark ran 870 trials across normal, fault, stress, and recovery cases. The normal suite passed fully, faults produced structured errors, and recovery worked for all three protocols.
arxiv-2603-24903: Rajamohan and co-authors assess self-supervised learning for knee osteoarthritis modelling. They compare image-only self-supervision on X-rays from three cohorts with multimodal image-text pretraining on hospital images paired with notes. For diagnostic grading, the results are mixed. Image-only pretraining helps under linear probing but not under full fine-tuning, and multimodal pretraining does not improve grading. The hospital corpus covers only confirmed cases, which limits grading signal. For prognostic modelling, though, the multimodal start improves performance, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-25003: Aslam and co-authors count lines that can cut a pair of twisted cubic curves. A general pair in complex space shares ten such secant lines. The team shows the symmetry group of those ten lines is the full symmetric group, so the lines have no hidden pattern. They then ask which of the ten can be real for real curves, and refine the count by where lines meet the curves. For each count from zero to ten, they build real pairs with exactly that many fully real common secants.
arxiv-2603-25303: Ben Mazziane and co-authors study learning in repeated proportional allocation auctions. In the Kelly scheme, a shared resource splits in line with bids. When bidders repeat the game with log-shaped payoffs, one stage has a single Nash equilibrium. The team proves play settles there under three habits: gradient descent, dual averaging, and plain best response. The result holds even when each bidder tunes a private learning rate. Simulations compare the habits. Best response settles fastest and earns most, while mixed habits can break convergence.
arxiv-2603-25703: McLeod, Pokraka, and Ren show that the wavefunction of the universe obeys a graphical coaction. Their setting is conformally coupled scalars in power-law FRW cosmologies. The coaction explains the full analytic structure of the wavefunction. It does so through the acyclic minors of Feynman graphs. The result holds for all particle counts and any loop order. One slice of it reproduces the kinematic flow behind the wavefunction's differential equations. Any discontinuity of a coefficient can also be read off from the coaction.
arxiv-2603-25803: Baxevanakis and co-authors retest whether all vision transformers need register tokens. An earlier study blamed attention map artifacts on a lack of space for global information. Adding empty register tokens cleared the artifacts in that work. This team repeats the tests on DINO, DINOv2, OpenCLIP, and DeiT3. They confirm several of the original claims. Other claims do not hold across all models, they find. They also extend the tests to smaller models. The authors clear up mixed terms in the first study and trace their effect on broad claims.
arxiv-2603-25903: Pan and co-authors present ENAP, a robot policy that learns symbolic structure from demonstrations. Long tasks are hard for end-to-end policies, which lack clear structure. Hand-built symbolic priors take expert effort. ENAP clusters the data and extends the L-star method to learn a Mealy state machine. That machine plans at a high level, in plain view. A reactive network then handles fine control by behavior cloning. In low-data tests, the authors report gains of up to 27 percent over top rival policies.
arxiv-2603-26003: Peralta introduces a new class of stochastic systems whose jump rates depend on the full past. In these hybrid equations with memory, rates look at the history of both the continuous and discrete parts. This allows age-based jumps and self-reinforcing dynamics. His Modular-Poisson algorithm draws jumps by path-dependent uniformization. Between jumps, any standard solver advances the continuous part. Peralta proves pathwise convergence with explicit rates. The proof controls error growth across regime changes. The design lets users plug in trusted solvers while keeping the guarantees.
arxiv-2603-26403: Luo and co-authors introduce T-800, a data glove that tracks full-hand motion at 800 Hz. Fast hand moves carry fine detail that slower systems miss, and camera setups suffer from blocked views. The glove syncs 18 inertial sensors spread across the hand with a broadcast scheme and a stress-isolating build. It holds sub-frame alignment through long, vigorous sessions. Their tests show dexterity holds strong motion energy above 100 Hz, and a retargeting method maps the gestures onto robot hands.
arxiv-2603-26503: Bolte, Pauwels, and Traoré prove an adjoint state formula for parametric optimisation without smoothness or unique solutions. The problems they cover can be nonconvex and definable, with nonsmooth goals and conic constraints. Even then, a mere qualification condition is enough for their formula to hold. The adjoint build yields a selection of a conservative field for the value function, a usable first-order object. Examples show the formal adjoint can fail without conservativity or definability, even in smooth cases.
arxiv-2603-27003: Mukherjee and co-authors reconstruct 3D heart shapes from routine MRI scans using a neural field method. Cardiac digital twins need accurate anatomy, but standard scans give sparse planar contours. Their framework learns a continuous shape representation from those contours. Tests used both simulated and real patient datasets with varied sampling. Reconstructed meshes closely matched the reference geometries in both. The method beat local interpolation most clearly at the apex and base. Gains were largest when contour sampling was sparse.
arxiv-2603-27203: Aguilera and co-authors use descriptive set theory to size up intervals of equational theories and logics. Coding equations by natural numbers turns collections of theories into sets of reals. Their Borel complexity can then be measured directly. Every interval of equational theories in a countable language is a Π⁰₁ set, they prove. Finite model property spans of normal modal logics are Π⁰₂ sets. Both kinds therefore have cardinality at most countable, or exactly continuum, provably in ZFC. Open problems from Jackson and Lee are settled along the way.
arxiv-2603-27403: Ye and co-authors build a guard against false claims from language models. Their method, called CFC, gives set-valued answers with coverage promises. A learned threshold adapts to how hard each prompt is. Easy prompts get small answer sets. Hard prompts get wider ones. The team proves the coverage claim under mild conditions. A stricter form adds a finite-sample safety bound. Tests on reasoning, question answering, and image tasks hit target coverage. The answer sets stay smaller than rival methods.
arxiv-2603-27703: Li and a large team present KAT-Coder-V2, an agentic coding model. Training splits skills into five expert domains first. Software, web, terminal, search, and general tasks train apart. Each expert gets supervised tuning plus reinforcement learning. On-policy distillation then merges them into one model. A sandbox system runs tens of thousands of sessions at once. Scores hit 79.6 percent on SWE-bench Verified. Frontend and terminal results also rank high.
arxiv-2603-27903: Loftus ties persistence diagrams of random matrices to their eigenvalues. A quadratic form on a sphere drives the filtration. Morse theory fixes the diagram by eigenvalue spacings. Bars count n minus one, each in its own dimension. Gaussian ensembles yield a closed-form persistence entropy. GOE, GUE, and Wishart classes leave distinct fingerprints. Persistence entropy beats spacing ratios at telling classes apart. AUC hits 0.978 versus 0.952 at size one hundred.
arxiv-2603-28103: Curini and three co-authors transcribe Italian parliamentary speeches from scanned pages using vision-language models. Older OCR pipelines left many errors and little semantic markup. Their pipeline pairs a specialized OCR model with a large vision-language model that fixes text, classifies elements, and names speakers. Speakers are then linked to the Chamber of Deputies knowledge base by fuzzy matching. On a benchmark, the method sharply improved both transcription quality and speaker tagging.
arxiv-2603-28203: Öz and five co-authors recast AC power flow as a differentiable simulation. The classic Newton-Raphson solver scales poorly just as grids grow more complex with renewables. Their Differentiable Power-Flow lets gradients run from power mismatches back to the model's parameters. GPU batching and sparse tensors make it fast, and old solutions can be reused across time steps. The tool suits time-series studies, contingency screening, and joint transmission and distribution models.
arxiv-2603-28403: Behrndt, Philipp, and Trunk characterize non-negative operators in Krein spaces, settings with an indefinite inner product. Heinz Langer's definitizable operators frame the area, and this subclass is a key special case. The new test reads local sign traits of the spectrum plus growth limits on the resolvent. From it they define local non-negativity for self-adjoint operators. Such operators turn out to arise naturally when non-negative ones are perturbed.
arxiv-2603-28903: Benvenuti, Rao, and Hale develop a differential privacy mechanism for symbolic trajectories. Such data are words over a finite alphabet, so noise adding tools do not apply. Their method picks an approximation to release in place of the word, biased toward low error ones. It builds on the permute-and-flip mechanism. A naive version would list exponentially many words, so they generate private words without such a list. They prove accuracy no worse than the prior state of the art. On traffic data, error fell by up to 55 percent.
arxiv-2603-29203: Brakensiek and co-authors propose a way to create dipolar supersolids in quantum gases. Their protocol sweeps a repulsive light barrier through a droplet array. The droplets start incoherent and quasi-one-dimensional. The team tracks density, momentum, and superfluid fraction during the sweep. A steady superfluid background appears under the crystals. The crystals then oscillate together, showing phase coherence. They map how barrier speed and height shape the effect. The scheme uses tools within current experimental reach.
arxiv-2603-29403: Al Masoud and co-authors present a systematization of knowledge on security in LLM-as-a-Judge systems. Such systems use strong language models to grade generated outputs. They speed up evaluation but add new security risks. Judges can be attacked, or used as tools for attacks. The team reviewed 863 works and kept 45 relevant studies. Their taxonomy sorts work by the judge's role in each attack or defense. They map open gaps and threats. The survey aims to guide safer judge design.
arxiv-2603-29503: Eugene and Neige use decades of Milky Way monitoring to watch the galaxy change in real time. Galaxies are usually seen at one frozen moment. Assembly plays out over the full age of the universe. The pair track three traits: the central black hole mass, the bar pattern speed, and the Sun's distance to the center. Archival data suggest all three shift surprisingly fast. The changes unfold over just a few decades. The authors speculate that shared physical processes drive them.
arxiv-2603-29603: Pérez-Cruz and co-authors study the superfluid response of a dilute bosonic fluid in composite light potentials. The potentials include triangular, Kagomé, and quasiperiodic patterns made from laser beams. They first find when the response must be fully isotropic. Then they derive Leggett's upper and lower bounds for the superfluid fraction. The formulas show the best direction to measure each bound. The bounds hold in the perturbative regime. Numerical solutions confirm the analytical results. The work maps how response direction matters in these traps.
arxiv-2603-29703: Uderzo studies solution maps tied to a family of parameterized split feasibility problems. These problems are convex and show up in engineering and systems biology. He uses tools from variational analysis to study how the map responds to small changes. He gives conditions for calmness, Lipschitz bounds, and the Aubin property. Each result comes with a quantitative estimate of the exact bound. The work aims to treat these related properties in one unified way.
arxiv-2604-00203: Honjani and Heidari study learning unitaries whose Pauli spectrum concentrates on at most s components with small residual, covering sparse unitaries, k-juntas, and near-Clifford compositions. Given query access to a unitary, their algorithm builds a close channel with query counts growing polynomially in sparsity and inverse accuracy. A key part estimates large Pauli coefficients up to a shared phase, extending sparse recovery to general unitaries. For bounded Pauli norm unitaries, they prove an exponential query lower bound, then show learnability under a relaxed metric for input states.
arxiv-2604-00303: Shelby builds a CubeSat cybersecurity framework, whose cheap designs create risks that NIST, ISO, and supply-chain guidance miss, since it assumes computing and governance that power-limited missions lack. A 42-entry register using STRIDE, ATT&CK, CVSS shows risks cluster in communication and ground segments. Security-per-Watt rates benefit for each unit of power, and a Distributed Security Paradigm treats incident response as an autonomous constellation function. Adapted controls give about 3 times the benefit for cryptography and about 2 times for incident response over terrestrial versions.
arxiv-2604-00503: Fu and colleagues propose PET-DINO, a universal detector for open-set object detection that accepts both text and visual prompts. Open-set detection must recognise new categories beyond fixed classes, but text alone aligns poorly with complex visual ideas, and image-text pairs are scarce for rare categories. Visual-prompted methods help only partly, with tangled multi-modal designs and multi-stage optimisation that slow development. PET-DINO's alignment-friendly visual prompt module builds on an advanced text-prompted detector to close those gaps.
arxiv-2604-01003: Syed, Wang, and Berloff show how multidimensional vector spins could strengthen analog hardware that minimizes Ising energy to solve combinatorial problems. They introduce a soft vector spin model for analog platforms, plus three dimensional annealing methods exploiting the enlarged phase space of vectorial degrees of freedom. Simulations on benchmark problems show vectorial degrees beat one-dimensional ones at finding the Ising ground state for every method tested. The edge grows sharpest at dimension 3 and above, then fades.
arxiv-2604-01103: Azevedo de Amorim, Kori and Muroya give a tool for bisimulations that judge when two reward-earning systems count as the same, tracking gaps in earned rewards. They pair a graded form, which caps reward gaps, with an ungraded form that ignores them, linking the two by categorical gluing. The build fits well with core coalgebra ideas such as final coalgebras and gives one shared account of both forms under mild rules. It spans link-based sameness for reward automata and gap-based sameness for labelled Markov processes.
arxiv-2604-01303: Aberlé builds a compositional framework for checking programs, using polynomial functors in dependent type theory as its backbone. Polynomial functors act as program interfaces, Kleisli maps for the free monad act as implementations, and dependent polynomials encode pre- and postcondition specs. Implementations and their proofs join through wiring diagrams, while Mealy machines supply a step-by-step operational meaning. The whole system is formalized in Agda as a proof of concept, with sketches toward concurrency and relational checking.
arxiv-2604-01403: Liu and colleagues prove two concentration inequalities for nonlinear stochastic systems under time-varying contraction. Their key tool is an energy function called the Averaged Moment Generating Function. With stability analysis, it bounds the gap between the noisy state and its deterministic twin. They then combine the function with martingale methods to bound the fluctuation of the whole trajectory. Combined, the two results improve the path bound for strongly shrinking systems, with a tight square-root-log bound shown in safe control.
arxiv-2604-02203: Romero and colleagues reframe cell cell communication as learning how interactions transform cell states. Their QuantumXCT model encodes transcriptomic profiles in a Hilbert space and trains quantum circuits to map a non interacting state to an interacting one, without leaning on curated ligand receptor tables. Tests on synthetic data and ovarian cancer fibroblast co cultures recover feedback loops and hub axes like PDGFB PDGFRB STAT3. The circuit topology itself translates into readable interaction networks.
arxiv-2604-02303: Gadouleau relates trapspaces and commutative Boolean networks in five steps. He introduces the trapping graph and trapping closure, defines trapping networks via transitive general asynchronous graphs, and proves they are exactly the trapping closures. Two networks share the same trapspaces exactly when they share the same trapping closure, and he lists the possible collections. Such networks prove trapping, with classified principal collections. Bijective and idempotent cases, called Marseille and Lille networks, each get full classifications.
arxiv-2604-02403: Espinal Maya sets conditions for language model scores to serve as valid scores for hidden economic traits, for task content beyond survey reach. Four govern validity: semantic exogeneity, construct relevance, monotonicity and model invariance. An Augmented Human Capital Index built from O*NET task items scored by Claude Haiku shows strong convergent and discriminant power. It spans two distinct axes, augmentation and substitution, with robust task rankings across prompt framings. IV results run 25 percent larger than OLS, consistent with measurement error.
arxiv-2604-02503: Grasev and Mendez identify a compact model for a variable-pitch propeller powertrain, covering the full chain from control signals to thrust. Their Wiener-style model passes the inputs through simple linear dynamics for the motor and pitch actuator, then maps the result through a fixed nonlinear relation to thrust. The model reproduces measured behavior accurately while staying interpretable and light enough for real-time digital twins and control.
arxiv-2604-02703: Yang studies nonlinear dispersive waves in the discrete modified Korteweg-de Vries equation. He simulates Riemann problems for rarefaction waves and dispersive shock waves. He offers distinct quasi-continuum models for the shapes and edge features of both wave types. A Whitham analysis then tracks how the parameters of periodic traveling waves drift slowly. That work yields a shock fitting method for edge traits. Both wave types get their own model. Numerical checks round out the study.
arxiv-2604-03203: MacRae and colleagues release PR3DICTR, a modular open framework for building prediction models from 3D medical images. Built on PyTorch and MONAI, it standardizes training while letting users plug in their own architectures and methods, and it handles any binary or event-based 3D classification task. A basic task needs just two lines of code to start.
arxiv-2604-03303: Dumont Le Brazidec and colleagues build a diffusion downscaler that turns coarse global forecast sets into high-resolution ones. Trained on ECMWF past forecast pairs, it learns fine-scale gaps from 100-kilometer fields to recover 30-kilometer detail, with tuning in noisy regimes to capture extremes. Tests show better probabilistic skill, true small-scale spectra, and true-to-physics wind-pressure links.
arxiv-2604-03603: Chicago Park and colleagues linked two image-rebuilding tools that both lean on denoisers, showing how score-based diffusion models can serve as priors inside plug-and-play methods without reverse sampling. Their stochastic version adds noise during rebuilding, which steadies work on badly underdetermined problems and helps the solver escape flat saddle points. Trials on multi-coil MRI scans and heavily masked photos beat standard plug-and-play methods.
arxiv-2604-03703: Boyu Jiang, Jiawei Shen, and Kexue Li established local and global well-posedness for inhomogeneous nonlinear wave equations, which ask whether solutions exist, stay unique, and depend steadily on their starting data. Combining Strichartz estimates with the contraction mapping principle, they worked in the energy-subcritical regime across two function-space settings. Their results extend and improve earlier work on general nonlinear wave equations.
arxiv-2604-03903: Alberto Alfarano and colleagues strengthened machine-learning attacks on Learning with Errors, a hard lattice problem behind much post-quantum cryptography. Earlier attacks recovered only sparse secrets, with up to 3 active bits in the cruel region on BKZ-preprocessed samples. Larger training sets plus repeated examples let the team recover denser secrets, following a power law linking attempts, data size, and repeats. A new stepwise regression technique then recovered the cool bits of the secret.
arxiv-2604-04003: Shichao Ye and team built a periodic dichotomy transformation from answers to Riccati and Lyapunov laws. Applied to linear square-cost optimal control, it gives a plain form for the optimal extremal. The paper gives a full account of it under fast-decay steady-keeping and can-be-seen guesses. The build offers a new tool for control theory, and it works for a wide class of time-varying linear systems with a repeating pattern.
arxiv-2604-04303: Jung, Kim and Kim study lopsided barred galaxies in IllustrisTNG TNG50. From 770 barred galaxies they pick 519 clearly barred ones in stellar mass maps, sorting bars into Lopsided, Perturbed, Symmetric and Indeterminate groups. Galaxies with asymmetric bars show denser gas near the bar, livelier star formation and more recent bar birth. Yet the steadiest divider across groups is the host's stellar mass distribution, with no link to bar size. Asymmetric bars seem to favour lighter galaxies and may settle into symmetry over time, though TNG50 holds more than nearby observations show.
arxiv-2604-04903: Barré finds the most tightly concentrated modes for a multimode fiber by minimizing total spatial spread across all unitary transforms of a given mode set. The result mirrors maximally localized Wannier functions from solid-state physics. Applied to the Laguerre-Gaussian basis of a graded-index fiber, with counts from 6 to 55, the modes form concentric rings with no imposed geometry. Spot sizes and shapes change from ring to ring in ways simple packing rules miss, and at large counts neither ring populations nor spot patterns stay regular.
arxiv-2604-05103: Easson and Falato present a historical optical foundation for vacuum Kerr-Schild spacetimes on a background, interpreted in double-copy language. A seed, built from the expansion and twist of the Kerr-Schild congruence, is harmonic. Its inverse obeys an eikonal equation and reconstructs the congruence. The stationary geometry is organized by a single complex seed. This seed furnishes a representative of the zeroth-copy data. Its part yields the Kerr-Schild profile, and its gradient generates the gauge-field strength.
arxiv-2604-05203: Kasibatla and six colleagues give choice-led coding, a workflow fronting design choices as the shared medium between coder and agent. Choices are clear and set, made live with the agent asking them, and traceable to code. They built Aporia, a probe tracking choices in an open Choice Bank, asking them through design questions, and coding each as a test suite checking code. A study of 14 coders showed choice-led teamwork kept coder and agent in sync and showed gaps to support coder choices.
arxiv-2604-05303: Lin, Moya, Qi, and Ye introduce Jeffreys Flow, a sampler for physical systems whose rough energy landscapes trap ordinary methods in single valleys. Standard Boltzmann generators lean on a one-sided divergence that collapses onto some modes and misses others. The team instead distils samples from parallel tempering runs under a symmetric Jeffreys divergence, balancing precise local fit against coverage of all modes. Tests on rugged multi-peaked benchmarks show the collapse suppressed, with faster exact importance sampling for quantum thermal states.
arxiv-2604-05403: Sun and Yao prove a guess of Banerjee, Bringmann, and Bachraoui about endless sets of congruences for a limit sequence tied to two-color partitions with limits. They build on the trio's modular-form work and a cited identity to prove the claims modulo 4 and 8. Their proof also yields two earlier guesses of Andrews and Bachraoui about Ramanujan-type congruences.
arxiv-2604-05503: Ang and six colleagues work out a closed expression for three-point correlations on the sphere in critical loop models, where primary fields carry legs and a momentum-like parameter. They validate it three ways: conformal bootstrap for four-point functions, lattice-model transfer-matrix checks, and probability via loop ensembles and Liouville gravity. The formula fills a missing piece for solving these models and links three routes into two-dimensional statistical physics.
arxiv-2604-05703: Chiba and five colleagues model helium and strontium ionization out of equilibrium to explain a strong absorption dip near 1 micrometer in kilonova AT2017gfo. About 1 percent helium or 1 to 10 percent strontium by mass in fast ejecta reproduces the feature, with strontium matching the solar r-process pattern. The fits point to low electron fraction and low entropy, and helium may flag elements beyond the third r-process peak.
arxiv-2604-05903: Oratis and three colleagues track spread from one particle-coated drop squeezed flat. Across grain sizes, grains barely slow spread, a shock the team explains with a model that ties surface transfer to the coated skin. The grain layer steers flow timing, blocking flow only once grains pack tight, which shows why coated drops so often fail to seal.
arxiv-2604-06003: Biswas and Singh give a necessary and sufficient condition for a holomorphic vector bundle over a smooth complex projective variety of dimension at least three to admit a holomorphic Lie algebroid connection. The condition settles when such a connection exists for any bundle on such a variety. The paper states the criterion for any bundle on such a variety, with no extra assumptions on the bundle.
arxiv-2604-06403: Vassileva, Koychev, and Boytcheva present a method for recognizing toxic habit named entities in Spanish clinical texts, for the ToxHabits Shared Task. Their team entered subtask 1, spotting substance use and abuse notes in clinical case reports and sorting them as Tobacco, Alcohol, Cannabis, or Drug. They tried several language-model approaches: zero-shot, few-shot, and prompt optimization. GPT-4.1 with few-shot prompting performed best in their experiments. Their method scored F1 0.65 on the test set, a promising result for non-English named entities.
arxiv-2604-06503: Chettih, Yagoub, and Bendaoud study unbounded truncated Toeplitz operators on model space, the function space tied to an inner function u. They examine operators of this kind that are closed and densely defined and that commute with modified compressed shifts. Results also cover properties of these operators concerning invertibility and self-adjointness.
arxiv-2604-06803: Benke and seven colleagues track a change in radio galaxy 3C 84's jet collimation profile. A 2003 plasma ejection in the southern jet offered a rare view of jet formation with VLBI. Their 2016 space-VLBI image at 22 GHz resolves the core at 58 microarcseconds, three years after the first. The source changed, confirming a limb-brightened jet, a counter-jet, and a flipped hotspot. Its collimation profile evolved from quasi-cylindrical to parabolic, as mini-cocoon pressure fell and stopped confining the jet, and the team constrained core and hotspot magnetic fields.
arxiv-2604-07003: Long, Liu, and Xu bring EmoMAS, a multi-agent setup for high-stakes feeling talks. Large models serve negotiation but cost much and raise privacy risks. Small models offer an option yet struggle with feeling moves. EmoMAS uses a Bayesian boss running game-theory, reward, and mind agents. It fuses insights to tune feeling shifts while tuning agent trust from feedback, learning plans without pre-training. New benchmarks test the system. Tests show EmoMAS models beat rivals while keeping ethics.
arxiv-2604-07103: Santos, Granjeiro, and Peixoto propose a new high order advection scheme on spherical Voronoi grids for weather and climate models. Such grids bend to fit local detail without rewiring the solver, but their ragged cells make robust high order transport hard to build. High order advection matters because it cuts fake spreading and keeps fine tracer shapes crisp. The authors extend k exact rebuilding from flat grids to the sphere, then test it on classic sphere cases and in a moist shallow water model that carries moisture tracers.
arxiv-2604-07503: Bala and colleagues construct Super-Grassmannians for n-point functions in N equals 2 to 4 superconformal theory in 3D. Superconformal invariance and R-symmetry appear manifest through delta functions. They test the form in N equals 2 and N equals 4 AdS4 Yang-Mills theories. In the N equals 2 case, they get the gluon correlator from the scalar correlator. For N equals 4, they build the operator in two ways. One reaches spin 2 from a spin-zero base. The other is CPT conjugate with spins zero, one half, and one, matching flat results.
arxiv-2604-07603: Johannsen studies hidden regularization and generalization in oversized neural nets in controlled tests. Old theory predicts severe overfitting for models with far more weights than samples, yet deep nets generalize well. He tests stochastic gradient descent across batches, flat versus sharp minima, the Neural Tangent Kernel, double descent, and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis. Findings show generalization hinges on design, tuning, and loss shape. Smaller batches yield lower test error and flatter minima, and sparse subnetworks with only 10 percent of weights stay within 1.15 points of full-model scores.
arxiv-2604-07703: Li and nine colleagues use JWST 15-micron observations from four programs aimed at ten M-dwarf systems to search for wide-orbit gas giants beyond 10 AU. Applying reference differential imaging for accurate PSF subtraction, they achieve 5-sigma contrast of 8.9 times 10^-4 to 6.2 times 10^-3 at 1 arcsecond and 1.2 to 9.1 times 10^-4 beyond 3 arcseconds. Assuming solar metallicity and a clear atmosphere, they are sensitive to Jupiter-sized planets near 233 K beyond 20 AU in systems 12.5 parsecs away. Archival MIRI imaging proves a powerful window into wide-orbit gas giants around M-dwarfs.
arxiv-2604-08303: Yildirim and Ferguson analyze stability and sensitivity under objective errors in model predictive game controllers. Model-based multi-agent control needs agents to model others' conduct strategically. Game-theoretic ideas often model emergent collective conduct of selfish agents, used in multi-agent control design. In model predictive games, an agent repeatedly solves a finite-horizon game to predict system conduct and plan control actions. When multiple agents use these controllers, built-in game models may misspecify goals through wrong estimates or guesses about other agents.
arxiv-2604-08703: Yu and five colleagues build a source grounded dataset for QoS-QoE translation, the link between measurable network conditions and user felt video quality. Prior findings scatter across papers and setups, so their automated pipeline curates papers, extracts relationships with definitions and evidence, and checks data in rounds. Language models fine tuned on the set predict both continuous values and discrete labels in both directions, giving a benchmark for multimedia quality work.
arxiv-2604-09003: Reinhardt and five colleagues review how global-scale collisions are modeled with smoothed particle hydrodynamics, a simulation method for impacts no lab can copy. Impacts shape Solar System bodies' physical and chemical traits, and modeling their material behavior, from shear strength and porosity to cracking, is key. The review lays out impact regimes and the physics each needs, then applies them to asteroids, comets, and other Solar System objects. It weighs recent sightings and models to sharpen our grasp of impacts and how the Solar System formed.
arxiv-2604-09303: Zhou, Liang, Lu, and Mou present an online framework for predicting the goal state of autonomous systems in real time. The problem is framed as inverse optimal control and inverse reinforcement learning, with intention as a parameter in the objective. A shifting horizon discounts outdated information, while control-informed learning enables efficient gradients and online updates. Simulations under varied noise and hardware tests on a quadrotor drone show accurate, adaptive prediction in complex settings.
arxiv-2604-09803: Saleem and six co-authors propose MAGE, a modality-agnostic framework for music generation and extraction in a shared latent space. Most systems handle one mode: generating without a mixture or extracting a source from one. MAGE's FluxFormer models the flow from noise to audio latents, with or without a mixture. Audio-Visual Nexus Alignment maps visuals onto audio latents, and cross-gated modulation lets visuals regulate audio features while text guides semantics. With dynamic modality masking, MAGE is tested on MUSIC, where alignment and gating cut interference in extraction.
arxiv-2604-09903: Tran and Kosecka present PointSplat, a geometry-driven prune-and-refine method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that bridges Gaussian pruning and transformer refinement. Most methods rank Gaussians from 2D images and fine-tune per scene; PointSplat ranks them from 3D attributes alone, removing any reliance on 2D images during pruning. A dual-branch encoder separates and re-weights geometry and appearance to avoid feature imbalance. Tests on ScanNet++ and Replica across sparsity levels show competitive rendering quality with superior efficiency, and no extra per-scene optimization.
arxiv-2604-10003: Dunham and five colleagues estimate protostar luminosities from limited infrared photometry, a route to masses and accretion, using radiative transfer models of collapsing cores. Luminosity links tightly in log-log space to 70-micron flux, but earlier estimates run low by factors of 2 to 3. Single wavelengths from 40 to 350 microns give factor of 3 uncertainty or less. At 70 to 160 microns, uncertainty tightens to factor 2 or less. Two simultaneous JWST filters beat the best single filter estimate; three match far-infrared accuracy.
arxiv-2604-10103: Li and six colleagues tackle streaming video generation, where sliding-window attention drops distant history and costs too much live. Their Hybrid Forcing design adds light linear temporal attention for long-range links beyond the window. A compact key-value state absorbs evicted tokens cheaply. Block-sparse attention trims waste inside the local window, and decoupled distillation trains the hybrid design in stable stages. The result generates unbounded 832 by 480 video live at 29.5 frames per second on one H100 card, with no quantization or compression.
arxiv-2604-10203: Gu, Ouyang, Jiang, and Zhang design analog beamforming and power allocation for a single radio-frequency chain multiuser time-division system under a max-min signal-to-noise criterion. A hardware-efficient phased array shares one beamforming vector across users under constant-modulus constraints. For any fixed beamformer, optimal power allocation follows in closed form, reducing the problem to phase-shift optimization alone. Globally optimal branch-and-bound algorithms handle discrete and continuous phase shifts. Tests show these algorithms reach the global optimum and benchmark low-complexity alternating-optimization methods.
arxiv-2604-10403: Easley and Farquhar retrain how language models read orders instead of only policing their acts. Their LIRA method shifts the inner grasp of a command, so malign prompts lose their grip. A self testing training loop pushes that shield further across fresh attack styles. The shield stops over 99 percent of PEZ jailbreak tries and wipes a hard unsafe code backdoor. It also reaches top marks for WMDP cyber forgetting while keeping benign skills nearly whole.
arxiv-2604-10503: Chauhan and Pundhir show mel scale audio fronts tilt against non Western ears. Mel scales rest on 1940s Western hearing tests, yet now sit inside nearly all audio tools. Their tests span speech in 11 tongues, music in 6 sets, and scenes in 10 European cities. Mel word error hits about 31 percent on tonal tongues versus about 19 percent on others. LEAF and ear shaped rivals shrink the gaps sharply, with CQT cutting music gaps by about half.
arxiv-2604-10603: Balderas, Lastra, and Benítez offer MoEITS, a method for slimming mixture-of-experts language models so they cost less compute, memory, and energy to train and run. Built on standard information-theory tools, it prunes expert models while keeping their accuracy, and the authors test it against leading pruning methods on Mixtral 8x7B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Their trials find MoEITS beats the rivals on both benchmark quality and efficiency, making large expert models cheaper to deploy.
arxiv-2604-10703: Cirrincione introduces INCRT, a transformer that settles its own architecture during training. Starting from one head, it adds heads when needed and prunes redundant ones. Each growth choice follows one geometric quantity from the task's structure, with no hand-tuned schedule. Two theorems back the design: convergence to a minimal sufficient setup and a cap on head count. Tests on SARS-CoV-2 classification and SST-2 sentiment match predictions within 12 percent. Final models match or beat BERT-base with three to seven times fewer parameters and no pretraining.
arxiv-2604-11003: Rewolinski and six colleagues propose two lightweight sanity checks for agentic data science, grounded in the PCS framework. Agentic systems can reach overly positive conclusions that users struggle to detect. The checks use changes to test whether an agent tells signal from noise. They can expose unsupported positive claims. Together they show whether an output found stable signal, responded to noise, or is sensitive to chance details. On eleven real datasets with OpenAI Codex, a positive conclusion proves unsupported in six, while reported confidence proves poorly matched to steadiness.
arxiv-2604-11203: Azatov and Missoni review how deuterium abundance measurements limit models of how matter won out over antimatter in the early universe. The review covers a range of models, old and new, and weighs each against the same data. Across most relevant settings, electroweak baryogenesis stays largely unconstrained by current and future deuterium-to-hydrogen data. Other models face much stronger limits, with some settings ruled out that would otherwise stay open.
arxiv-2604-11403: Lino and Thuerey sample unsteady fluid flows scale by scale with scale-autoregressive modeling. Instead of stepping a learned solver forward, with errors compounding, or paying for many evaluations across the whole mesh, their method first generates a coarse field. It then refines that field through progressively finer resolutions conditioned on coarser predictions. Concentrating compute where uncertainty is greatest yields lower distributional error and higher per-sample accuracy than multi-scale diffusion baselines, while matching or beating a flow-matching Transolver at two to seven times its speed.
arxiv-2604-11503: Ramsey, McKeown, and Palastro show how to build a charged-lepton wavepacket whose density peak travels at any chosen speed. Imposing momentum links among Volkov states shapes a wavepacket in space and time whose peak speed is set apart from the field strength and the mean velocity. The links also shift the mean path, giving a measurable sign of the chosen speed in a real observable.
arxiv-2604-11603: Kirkby, Chomaz, and Gasenzer study false-vacuum decay between two distinct supersolid phases in a dipolar gas in a plane. Starting from a honeycomb state, stripe domains form by bubble nucleation, simulated with a stochastic Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Bubble growth speed is set by the slowest of the supersolid's multiple sound speeds. The decay rate is extracted and compared with a model for the Coleman bounce solution linking the two orders. Dipolar supersolids thus offer a versatile platform for false-vacuum decay, with bubbles visible directly in real-space density.
arxiv-2604-11803: Oberkircher, Alabi, Klakow, and Trouvain build Saar-Voice, a six-hour speech corpus for the Saarbrücken dialect of German, drawn from digitised books and local material and recorded by nine speakers. They analyse both text and audio, discuss spelling and speaker variation, and explore converting letters to sounds. The aligned text and audio aim to support dialect-aware speech synthesis, especially where training data are scarce.
arxiv-2604-11903: Morras, Pratten, Schmidt, and Buonanno present pyEFPEHM, a post-Newtonian (PN) waveform model for eccentric, precessing binaries with higher modes and matter effects. Above 2.5PN order, quasi-circular terms rule phasing at each order, and the model adds all those corrections, including tidal effects. Corrections for eccentricity reach first PN order in signal amplitudes across a mode set. Checked against formula models and computer runs, it stays robust and fast until near merger, failing only late for very unequal masses, large aligned spins, or very stretched orbits.
arxiv-2604-12203: Takahashi and three colleagues apply the spherical-tensor formalism from nuclear physics to the Mott phase of A3C60. The model is a single-site system with many orbitals coupled to Jahn-Teller vibrations. Both the standard quadrupole moment and the lattice displacement vanish, despite extra freedoms implied by the degenerate ground multiplet. Two-body quadrupole operators mixing electrons and phonons fill the gap. Quasispin rules show the mixed form does not couple to either standard one.
arxiv-2604-12403: Jungwon Choi and Eunwoo Kim improve test-time prompt tuning for vision-language models. It adapts a model from augmented views of a test image. Standard filters trust the model's own confidence, which misfires under distribution shift. Empty crops can outscore meaningful ones. Their method anchors view choice in attribute-rich text descriptions. An evolving image anchor adds test-time statistics. Anchor predictions blend with the model's output for steadier supervision. Tests on 15 benchmarks set a new state of the art.
arxiv-2604-12503: Shuai Wang and two colleagues reason over incomplete knowledge graphs with soft prompts. Most multi-hop methods walk graph edges step by step, so missing edges break them. Their framework encodes whole subgraphs into soft prompts with a graph neural network. The model then reasons over richer structure and spots entities beyond near neighbors. A light model first picks relevant entities and relations. A stronger model then writes evidence-aware answers. The method leads on three of four multi-hop benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-12603: Nora Brambilla and three colleagues revisit open-flavor threshold effects on the quarkonium spectrum. The team uses Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory. Within that theory, threshold effects come from mixing of quarkonium and tetraquark potentials. Tetraquark potentials repel nearby and approach meson thresholds far away. Coupled Schrödinger equations with the adjoint meson mass as sole free parameter give below-threshold effects. Spin splittings of real thresholds appear for the first time. Results are validated as self-energy corrections and compared with data.
arxiv-2604-12803: Adam T. Müller and two colleagues anonymize event-camera streams without wrecking their usefulness. Video models can rebuild face images from sparse events, leaking identities in public spaces. Masking or scrambling breaks the space-time structure that later vision tasks need. Their pipeline turns events into an image, swaps in a fake identity, and re-encodes the result as events. Identity recovery is blocked while structure for later tasks survives. A new synchronized event and RGB set from robot paths gives future work a benchmark.
arxiv-2604-13103: Yang-Smith, de Souza Santos, and Abdellatif review fairness in multi-agent systems used across software development, screening 350 papers down to 18 studies. Fairness appears as trusted AI principles, bias reduction across groups, and interaction dynamics in teams, while harms span representation, service quality, security and privacy, and governance. Three gaps persist: fragmented evaluation, narrow settings and attributes, and scarce, weakly tested mitigation, leaving the field unready for deployable fairness-assured systems.
arxiv-2604-13303: Bowman studies smooth behaviour for solutions of a degenerate elliptic equation whose coefficients may decay, with only a weak integrability rule on the lower bound. He proves better oscillation control and a Liouville result when the exponent tops dimension minus one, plus a Harnack inequality for large exponents. He also proves a new log weak Harnack inequality and a local maximum rule. Examples show no such inequalities hold below the threshold.
arxiv-2604-13403: Wang and Li analyse why multimodal in-context learning lags behind text-only in-context learning. With identical tasks across modalities, multimodal learning matches text-only learning with no examples but degrades sharply with few-shot examples. They split the process into building a task mapping and transferring it to queries, tracking both across layers. Models lack alignment at the reasoning level between visual and textual representations, and they move mappings to queries unreliably. A simple inference-stage fix that reinforces transfer improves the process.
arxiv-2604-13803: Shah and three colleagues ask whether models whose visual representations mirror human brains resist sycophancy better. They evaluate 12 open-weight models across six model families and a wide parameter range. Brain alignment comes from fMRI responses, and sycophancy from 76,800 two-turn gaslighting prompts. Alignment in early visual cortex, areas V1 through V3, reliably predicts less sycophancy, with the strongest effect for existence denial attacks. Higher-order category regions show no such link. Faithful low-level visual encoding thus anchors models against word-based override.
arxiv-2604-13903: Connor and colleagues describe CASM-256, a dense array of 256 antennas now being deployed at Owens Valley Radio Observatory to watch the whole sky at 375 to 500 megahertz. Its wide field of about 10,000 square degrees should catch nearby fast radio bursts, ideal for tracing their origins, weighing nearby galaxy halos, and finding prompt counterparts. Early data from the first two dozen antennas already feed a live GPU burst search.
arxiv-2604-14103: Pinheiro and Almeida study chiral fermion zero modes trapped in a two-kink scalar background, a Jackiw-Rebbi realization from a deformed phi-fourth model. The modes' collective center moves linearly with the asymmetry parameter, tuning the effective brane position continuously. Meanwhile the separation between the two chiral modes blows up inversely as the background collapses to a single kink. Bilayer graphene under an asymmetric two-kink potential offers a concrete test platform.
arxiv-2604-14303: Hu's team of eight studies correlated excitations in twisted bilayer graphene near integer fillings, using the topological heavy-fermion model. In the decoupled limit, without hybridization or Hund coupling, free Dirac fermions live beside interacting f electrons in zero-width Hubbard bands. Treating both couplings as tweaks yields analytical self-energies, giving dispersion renormalization and scattering rates for Hubbard-band states and low-energy Dirac modes. Gamma3 and Gamma1,2 Dirac kinds scatter by own routes, and the results match dynamic mean-field results for the same model.
arxiv-2604-14403: Killingback and four colleagues move retrieval-augmented generation onto the device, dodging server privacy risks, upkeep costs, lag, and the need for a connection. On-device runs must squeeze the context fed to the generator and the stored embeddings, so the team unifies retrieval and context compression in one shared model. With one-tenth the context, their model matches a standard server-style reader without adding storage over a multi-vector retriever. The work first joins retrieval and compression this way, pointing toward leaner on-device systems.
arxiv-2604-15003: Chen and five others present Flow of Truth, the first proactive framework for time-based forensics in image-to-video generation. Static-image checks localize 2D pixel tampering, but video frames evolve, so traces drift and deform and spatial methods fail. They redefine generation as pixel motion through time rather than frame synthesis, with a learnable template following pixel motion and a flow module separating motion from content. The method generalizes across commercial and open-source image-to-video models, substantially improving temporal forensics performance.
arxiv-2604-15103: Lu and colleagues measure metal content for 367324 stars in Omega Centauri, the most massive and chemically varied globular cluster known. From Hubble colors they derive stellar loci, color patterns tied to metal content and brightness, then build a catalog of 20778 giants and 346546 dwarfs. A giant subsample shows no strong metallicity gradient inside the half-light radius, and an earlier ring-like pattern fades in the new data. The catalog greatly widens the cluster's metallicity sample and the method can travel to other Hubble data.
arxiv-2604-15203: Agarwal and colleagues launch MADE, a living benchmark for multi-label classification of medical-device adverse-event reports. Older benchmarks are saturating and may leak training data, blurring reasoning and memorization. MADE draws on continuously added published reports with strict time-based splits and a long-tailed hierarchy of labels. Baselines across over 20 models show clear trade-offs: small tuned decoders lead on accuracy, generative tuning gives the steadiest uncertainty, and self-stated confidence proves unreliable.
arxiv-2604-15303: Eberhard and three colleagues prove a general bound on the diameter of any finite group. The bound rests only on composition-factor diameters and the largest exponent of a normal abelian section. Uses include a diameter bound for soluble groups, polylogarithmic diameter for anabelian groups of bounded rank, and progress on Grigorchuk's gap conjecture for groups acting on bounded-degree trees.
arxiv-2604-15603: Ronggon and Farheen split quantum error budgets with a potential game, where Nash equilibrium gives a Pareto-optimal share for logic steps, T-state distillation, and rotation synthesis. Iterated best responses converge by steady descent of the shared cost. Across 433 MQT benchmarks, hardware needs fall 30.22 percent on average versus even shares, peaking at 97.81 percent for single circuits.
arxiv-2604-16003: Cao and five colleagues examine a virtual supporter in remote psychotherapy sessions held over Zoom. A formative study first mapped the roles of human supporters in therapy. The team then built a virtual supporter with two modes: Daily Mode for mood journaling outside therapy, and Therapy Mode as an extra participant in sessions. Fourteen participants used it for a week before joining a remote therapy session with it. It aided psychological safety, eased anxiety, and improved emotional articulation without disrupting therapy, though over-reliance and boundary concerns remain.
arxiv-2604-16203: Bark, Malik, Prus, Piepho, and Schmid propose a Bayesian framework for long-term multi-environment crop trials, where variety performance is tested across many sites. Estimating variance components is hard: standard restricted maximum likelihood often shrinks them to zero or gets them wrong, and rich historical data usually go unused. Their Bayesian linear mixed model uses priors and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling to keep variance components positive and quantify uncertainty better.
arxiv-2604-16403: Kommers and colleagues argue that generative AI should be judged as a cultural technology, not merely as a measuring instrument. Drawing on hermeneutic theory, they describe such systems as context machines facing three interpretive challenges: meaning depends on situation, several readings can be valid at once, and readings can conflict. Their computational hermeneutics framework calls for evaluations that repeat rather than run once, involve people alongside machines, and measure cultural context rather than output alone. The paper shifts the question from accuracy to meaning.
arxiv-2604-16903: Zhang, Huang and Ye present a gamey Unity framework for getting embodied interaction data at scale. Old screens limit reach, making large-scale body data collection costly and hard. The tool mixes procedural scene generation, VR-based human-like robot control, auto task scoring and trajectory logging. The trash pick-and-place demo proves the workflow, with demonstrations broadly spanning the state-action space. Harder tasks raise motion heat and widen arm workspace exploration, showing game virtual worlds serve body data collection.
arxiv-2604-17203: Leppänen, Nakajima, and Nakano study random open systems built from Lasota-Yorke maps, where trajectories escape through holes and the ensemble loses mass. They adapt functional correlation bounds from closed systems to open systems using Lasota-Yorke inequalities to control escapes. They establish an exponentially decaying bound. With normal-approximation results, it yields a conditional central limit theorem with Wasserstein rates and a conditional functional version with an integral-distance rate over Barbour's test functions. Tikhomirov's method also yields a Kolmogorov-distance bound on the conditional central limit theorem.
arxiv-2604-17303: Kuchař and Marek offer a leaner way to check Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits, the error-resistant building blocks proposed for quantum computers. Instead of costly full tomography, they build one test operator for each point on the qubit's Bloch sphere, whose measured value flags non-Gaussian character and doubles as twice the logical error rate. Only three quadrature measurements are needed, so the scheme suits both lab checks and tuning of state-preparation circuits.
arxiv-2604-17403: Kannan and five colleagues investigate compressional sound waves in cell culture media measured with a quartz crystal microbalance. Classical theory expects mainly shear waves, but finite liquid depth and reflections produce longitudinal waves that strongly shift resonance frequency and resistance. In DMEM and RPMI-1640, droplet volume drives the pattern: small drops oscillate slowly, about once per 40 minutes, while larger volumes oscillate about once per 5 minutes. Peak shifts and a phase lag near 10 minutes complete the picture, warning that such artifacts must be accounted for when cells are present.
arxiv-2604-17703: Kjos-Hanssen examines Carmo and Jones' sequence of candidate axiom systems for conditional obligation from 1997 to 2022. For their most recent system, he demonstrates a limited form of deontic explosion. When a student misses the top grade on a test, every other passing grade counts as acceptable. Alongside that negative result, he gives a positive one. Returning to Carmo and Jones' strongest 1997 system, he provides an unexpected classification of all satisfying models through one forbidden possible world.
arxiv-2604-18203: Balter, Ethan Jerzak, and Connor Jerzak test whether multimodal language models can actually multiply across text, image, and audio inputs. Models perceive numbers well in every modality yet fail at exact multi-digit multiplication. The authors build a paired benchmark varying digit length, sparsity, representation, and modality, and define arithmetic load C from total and nonzero digit counts. Accuracy falls sharply as C grows, nearing zero past 100, while perception checks stay near-perfect, showing the failure is computational, not perceptual.
arxiv-2604-18303: Hytönen and three colleagues develop a real-variable Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin theory with Ap weights. This covers phi-transform characterizations and almost diagonal boundedness. A key tool is a reverse Hölder version following from the Ap condition. They strengthen Hilbert-space no-go claims: every infinite-dimensional Banach space has an Ap weight with unbounded Hilbert transform. They achieve this by combining two methods in K-convex and non-UMD spaces.
arxiv-2604-18403: Lyon and Orlandelli build cut-free nested sequent systems for Horn-characterizable quantified modal logics with equality. The logics use link-based models giving each world an inner and an outer domain, letting frame conditions encode growing, shrinking, constant, and empty domains. Term bundles, called signatures, extend nested sequents to capture those rules. Reachability rules, tuned by formal grammars, spread or consume claims along grammar-made paths, yielding sound and complete systems with cut removal.
arxiv-2604-18803: Jiang and ten colleagues present Ghost-100, a benchmark of 800 images in eight categories and three task families, where each target is absent, illegible, or indeterminate by design. Every image pairs with five prompts from a five level intensity framework, varying only directive force so tone alone varies. A dual track protocol measures crossing from grounded refusal to unsupported commitment, and the confidence of fabrication once it occurs. Across nine open weight vision language models, the two measures dissociate, and several models peak in sensitivity at intermediate tone levels.
arxiv-2604-18903: Hmidhi and Fekih-Salem study the AM2 model in two linked chemostats run at distinct dilution rates. With distinct rates, the usual reduction from eight dimensions to four no longer works. They map all steady states and give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence, multiplicity, and local stability of nine equilibrium types. Coexistence equilibria with two species in the second bioreactor can exist yet stay unstable without an extra Jacobian trace condition. Finding Hopf bifurcations and limit cycles remains open.
arxiv-2604-19103: Brynes and four colleagues propose a generic format for describing particle accelerator lattices. Common formats let researchers share workflows, reuse generic tools, and cross-check results, but no standard lattice format exists yet. Their schema covers simulation parameters, control variables, and electrical and magnetic data. A translation layer exports the lattice for standard simulation codes. The framework generates, tracks, and analyzes beams through the lattice, moving smoothly between codes toward fully generic start-to-end simulation.
arxiv-2604-19303: Cavenaghi, Grama, Katzarkov, and Muniz Martins study the geometric and cohomological traits of non-Kähler SYZ mirror symmetry for dual torus fibrations over solvmanifolds.
